chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding the fasting one who rinses his mouth and inhales (water into the nose), he said: 'Yes, but he should not be excessive (in swallowing the water).'
ai.seo_question: Does rinsing the mouth and inhaling water break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that rinsing the mouth and inhaling water into the nose do not invalidate the fast, provided one avoids excessive force that leads to swallowing. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor actions during ablution or eating do not break the fast unless they result in the deliberate or accidental ingestion of water, distinguishing between the act itself and its consequence. The emphasis on 'not being excessive' (la yubaligh) highlights the importance of moderation in ritual purity practices while fasting.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from the one who mentioned it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Fasting one rinsing his mouth and inhaling. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but he should not swallow’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who rinses his mouth and nostril when he is fasting. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so but he must not swallow it.’”
